It is as if you were to say, "that well-known and notorious deceiver," who substituted one daughter for another as a bride for his son-in-law <note>Referring to Laban tricking Jacob into marrying Leah instead of Rachel</note> and changed his wages ten times. They observe something similar in the words of Jacob in Genesis 32:4, where he says: "Thus says your servant Jacob, 'I have **sojourned** <note>original: גַּרְתִּי (*Garti*)</note> with Laban.'" They explain this partly literally and partly through Kabbalistic methods as follows: **"I did not become a prince or a person of importance, but remained only a stranger; I do not see the benefit of the blessings your father gave me when he said 'Be lord over your brother,' for that has not been fulfilled in me. For he had a dispute with him. He was a man of strife and a master of war, and all this was to frighten him. "I have sojourned" <note>original Hebrew: גרתי (*Garti*)</note> in Gematria <note>A system where Hebrew letters are assigned numerical values</note> is 613. This is to say: "I have sojourned with Laban the wicked, yet I kept the 613 commandments and did not learn from his evil deeds." The meaning is: *I have lived as a stranger with Laban, that is, I did not become a Prince or an honored man (as you did, my brother Esau), but remained a traveler of lower status. Therefore, there is no reason for you to pursue me with hatred because of the blessing of your father, who blessed me thus in* Genesis 27:29: *“Be lord over your brothers.” That blessing has not yet come to pass for me.* 

Another way of explaining it: if you invert the word <term>Garti</term> <note>Hebrew: גרתי, meaning "I sojourned"</note>, it contains within itself the word <term>Tigri</term> <note>Hebrew: תגרי, meaning "strife" or "combatant"</note>, which refers to a quarrel, a dispute, or someone who is pugnacious, such as he was with Laban. For a dispute intervened between him and Laban; it is as if Jacob wanted to say, "I also know how to handle disputes and wars," specifically to strike terror into Esau by this reasoning. 

Again, another interpretation: <term>Garti</term> <note>גרתי</note> amounts to 613 through **Gematria** (the same number of commandments they say are in the Law). From this, Jacob wanted to say: *I have lived until now with that wicked Laban, yet I did not learn his evil works; rather, I kept all 613 commandments.*

XLI. In the writing of words, the **Kabbalists** pay the greatest attention to whether a word is written "fully" or "defectively." If it is written fully, it is called <term>Malei</term> <note>original: מלא, meaning "full" or "complete"</note>; if it is written defectively, it is called <term>Chaser</term> <note>original: חסר, meaning "missing" or "lacking"</note>, especially in the notes of the **Masorah** <note>The traditional system of notes used to preserve the exact text of the Hebrew Bible</note>...

...in these Masoretic notes. Let us take an example from Genesis 1:14, 15, and 16. There, the word <term>me'orot</term> <note>meaning "lights" or "luminaries"</note> is written defectively <note>original: מארת; "defective" spelling refers to Hebrew words written without certain vowels like the letter "vav" which acts as an "o" or "u" sound</note>, that is, without the letter *vav*; however, it is written completely elsewhere as <term>me'orot</term> <note>original: מאורות</note>. They provide this reason for the spelling:

> The word <term>me'orot</term> is written defectively because the Sun alone was created to illuminate the world; the Moon, however, was created only so that men might be discouraged from the worship of the Sun, lest they perceive it to be the sole great luminary if it were alone. For this reason, the word <term>me'orot</term> <note>spelled without the *vav*</note> through **Gematria** <note>The mystical system of assigning numerical values to Hebrew letters</note> very nearly matches the word *Shemesh* <note>Sun</note>. For the former in numbers totals 641, while the latter totals 640.

XLII. We have another example in 2 Kings 5:20, where the servant of Elisha <note>named Gehazi</note>, complaining that his master accepted nothing from Naaman the Syrian in exchange for curing his leprosy, says: *"As the Lord lives, if I do not run after him, I will take **something** from him"* <note>original Hebrew: מאומה (*me'umah*)</note>. The **Masorah** <note>The body of traditional notes and rules for the correct writing and reading of the Hebrew Bible</note> added this note: *The letter Aleph is missing according to the exposition of Rabbi Solomon Jarchi* <note>A famous 11th-century French rabbi, better known as Rashi</note>. Furthermore, the gloss of that Master is this:

> The word <term>me'umah</term> <note>meaning "something"</note> is written defectively without the letter *Aleph* <note>resulting in the word "muma"</note> because this taking of Naaman’s goods resulted in a **mum** <note>original: מום, meaning "blemish" or "stain"</note> to him.

For it is normally written fully as <term>me'umah</term> <note>original: מאומה</note>, meaning "something." But because of that crime, Gehazi was infected with leprosy, as were his descendants.

XLIII. It is fitting to also attach this point regarding the letter **Jod** <note>The tenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet, often used as a vowel or a plural marker</note>, which is found in **2 Samuel 18:18**: *"Absalom set up a monument for himself **in his life**"* <note>original: בחיי (*be-hayyav*)</note>, that is, while he was still living. This word *be-hayyav* is written "defectively" <note>meaning a letter is missing from its standard spelling</note>, and the Rabbis assign a cause for this—particularly **David Kimchi in his Commentary** <note>A famous 12th-century Hebrew grammarian and biblical scholar also known as the Radak</note>:

> <gloss>The word "his life" [chayav] is missing the *Jod* of the plural. In this is a hint that ten years were subtracted from the life of Absalom because he lay with the ten concubines of his father; therefore, it lacks the *Jod*, which stands for the number ten.</gloss>

That is to say: *In the word "be-hayyav" <note>original: בחיי</note> the Jod is missing, which is the sign of the plural number* (for it should have been written as *be-hayyav* <note>original: בחייו</note> with a double *Jod*, one being part of the root word and the other acting as a grammatical marker). *There is truly a mystical explanation in this matter: for ten years were subtracted from Absalom's life because he had relations with his father's ten concubines*, as recorded in **2 Samuel 15:26** and **16:22**. *This, I say, is the reason for the missing letter Jod, which in the system of numbers represents ten.* So much for the missing letters **Aleph**, **Vav**, and **Jod**; the remaining practices of the **Kabbalah** <note>The Jewish mystical tradition of interpreting the underlying meaning of the Torah</note> will provide more.

XLIV. I will now approach those words that produce a different reading, which fall into two—or rather three—categories of difference. For some readings are truly "variants," where the manuscripts have suffered some damage due to the injury of time and the frequent exiles of the Jewish people; however, the deficiency was carefully supplied by later generations from other copies. The sign for these is **Keri ve-lo Ketiv** <note>original: קרי ולא כתיב</note>, which means *"read but not written"*; likewise, **Ketiv ve-lo Keri** <note>original: כתיב ולא קרי</note>, which means *"written but [not] read."* <note>These are Masoretic notes in the margins of the Hebrew Bible that correct or clarify the text without altering the sacred original letters</note>

The word *shanim* <note>original Hebrew: שנים</note> indicates this. However, do not read it as *shanim*, that is, "years" <note>original Hebrew: שָׁנִים</note>, but as *shenayim*, that is, "two" <note>original Hebrew: שְׁנַיִם</note>. This suggests that two Prophets uttered the same prophecy at the same time. Here, Galatino <note>Pietro Galatino (c. 1460–1540), a Franciscan scholar who used Jewish literature to argue for Christian doctrines</note> does not warn of any corruption of the text. When the Rabbis say *al tikrei* <term>Al-tikrei: A traditional rabbinic formula meaning "do not read [the text this way], but [read it that way]," used to draw out a secondary, homiletic meaning without discarding the literal text</term>, the intention is not that the original and accepted reading should be removed. Rather, it means that if you substitute different vowel points, a sense is produced that perfectly suits the author's purpose. Thus, it marks a sharpness of insight <note>The author is defending the Rabbis against the charge of falsifying the Bible, explaining that their wordplay is a clever interpretive tool, not a claim that the written text is wrong</note>, not a falsification of the text.

LI. The same Galatino, in *Book 1, Chapter 8*, cites a passage from *1 Kings 12:16* as if it had been falsified by the Jews. The words of the text are these: *“What portion have we in David? We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse. "What portion have we in David?" as it is understood: "To your tents, O Israel." ...explains this: why one should not say *Moshe Rabbeinu* <note>original Hebrew: משה רבינו</note> (**"Moses our Teacher"**), but rather *Rabbeinu Moshe* <note>original Hebrew: רבינו משה</note> (**"Our Teacher Moses"**). LVI. **They are accustomed to examine the beginning and the end of verses**, whether they end with the same letter with which they began, or with a different one, as in **Genesis 19:23**: "The sun <note>original Hebrew: השמש (*Ha-shemesh*)</note> was risen upon the earth when Lot entered Zoar" <note>original Hebrew: צערה (*Tzoarah*)</note>. In the **Zohar** <note>The primary text of Jewish mysticism, the Cabbala.</note> it is written: *This verse begins with the letter He and ends with the letter He. This teaches that Lot traveled five miles before the sun rose.* That is, the verse begins with ה and ends with ה, and thus teaches that Lot traversed five miles before the sun arose <note>In Hebrew numerology, the letter 'He' (ה) represents the number five.</note>.

Likewise, in **Numbers 31:4**: "A thousand <note>original Hebrew: אלף (*Eleph*)</note> men from every tribe shall be chosen from Israel, whom you shall send to the war" <note>original Hebrew: לצבא (*la-tzava*)</note>. The verse begins with *Aleph* and ends with *Aleph* to teach that **they all possessed a single heart directed toward their Father in Heaven.** <note>The letter Aleph (א) is the first letter of the alphabet and represents unity or the number one.</note> That is, the verse begins with א and also ends with א.

...they have the **Mappiq** <term>a small dot placed in the Hebrew letter 'He' (ה) at the end of a word to indicate it should be pronounced and usually marks a possessive "her" or "it"</term>. One example has already been brought forward; the remaining two texts appear in **Ruth 2:14** and **Zechariah 5:11**. **Baal Hatturim** <term>Jacob ben Asher, a 14th-century scholar famous for his commentary on the Torah using mystical and numerical methods</term> turns to the **Cabbala** <term>the Jewish mystical tradition of inner scriptural interpretation</term> with these words:

**לה ג׳ לה : קלח לה כוכב לה ויקרא לה בשמו סלה נתקיים לה זה המס-תר לבנות לה בית בארץ שנער מבקש לבנות ולא זכה ויאמר לה בועז סלה דבר עמה הוא בעצמו אלא על ידי שליח לה כמו לא :**

In **Numbers 32, the final verse**, the Mappiq is missing to serve as a sign that this place-name did not remain for long, as another name was given to it shortly thereafter. 

In **Zechariah 5:11**, the angel says: "To build **לה** <note>original: *lah*, "for it"</note> (referring to the **Ephah** <note>a measuring basket appearing in Zechariah’s vision</note>) a house in the land of Shinar." Indeed, the absence of the Mappiq indicates that although they desired to build there, they did not actually erect a house in that place. 

Finally, in **Ruth 2:14**, the same dot is missing in the word **לה** to indicate that **Boaz** did not speak with **Ruth** in his own person, but rather through a certain intermediary. LX. They likewise refer the **substitution of number** <term>enallage; a grammatical shift where a singular form is used instead of plural, or vice-versa</term> to a mystical interpretation, and they maintain that it denotes two things above all others:

I. The dignity of the person speaking. For example, in **Numbers 32[:25]**:
<note>original Hebrew: ויאמר בני גד היה לו לומר ויאמרו אלא הגדול שבכולם דבר בשביל כולם</note>
"And the sons of Gad **spoke**" <note>In the original Hebrew, the verb *vayomer* (and he spoke) is singular, while "sons of Gad" is plural</note>. That is to say: although the text has "and he spoke, the sons of Gad," it ought to have been in the plural, "and they spoke." Therefore, by this discrepancy in number, it is indicated that the most distinguished or the greatest of the sons of Gad spoke on behalf of all the rest.

II. The consensus of the others, as in **Numbers 33[:7]**:
<note>original Hebrew: ויסעו מאתם וישב על פי החירות והיה לו לומר וישובו מלמד שכולם היה להם לב אחד לעשות כן על פי צווי המקום</note>
"And they departed from Etham, and **he turned back** <note>original Hebrew: *vayashav*, singular</note> toward Pi-Hahiroth." That is to say: when it says, "and they departed from Etham, and he turned back," the text teaches—by using the singular where it should have said "and they turned back"—that they all had one heart to execute this, or to bring it to effect, and indeed according to the command of Moses himself <note>The Hebrew text uses the phrase "the command of the Place," a common rabbinic title for God; however, the Latin translator interprets this as the command of Moses.</note>.

LXI. Finally, they are also accustomed to counting the letters; for example, in the first verse of the first chapter of **Leviticus**, there are:
<note>original Hebrew: ויקרא א' קטנה וידבר יהוה אליו מאהל מועד לאמר חמשה אלפי"ם כנגד חמשה חומשי תורה ותשעה תיבות יש בו וכן יש תשעה תיבות הפסוק לקרבן לה' אלהיך לומר שכל הלומד תורה כאילו הקריב כל הקרבנות וכן תשעה תיבות בפסוק זות תורת העולה</note>
A **small Aleph** <term>the letter א, written smaller than the surrounding text in the first word of Leviticus, *Vayikra*</term> in the verse: "And the Lord called to him and spoke to him from the tent of meeting, saying..." There are, I say, five **Alephs** <note>the letter א</note> in this verse, which correspond to the five books of the **Torah** <term>the Law, or the Pentateuch</term>. Furthermore, there are nine words in this verse. In the same way, there are nine words in the verse regarding "an offering to the Lord your God," to suggest that whoever studies the Torah is as if they had offered all the sacrifices. Similarly, there are nine words in the verse, "This is the law of the burnt offering."

### *On the Use of Kabbalah in Theology, Whether Jewish or Christian.*

LXIV. Indeed, I judge the use of this study to be most clearly evident in the topic and controversy concerning the Messiah. Since the Jewish authorities derive this form of their learning from their most pious ancestors—even involving the Prophets—and since even modern writers frequently wish to wrest the sayings about the Messiah from our hands, it would be worthwhile to investigate the expositions of those who speak on this same matter outside the heat of dispute. We should reveal what they once kept secret and compare these ideas with the writings of the New Testament. However, due to the shortness of time, I will carry this out in a somewhat hurried manner rather than in a proper order, speaking now of the Messiah’s person, and now of his office <note>The "office" refers to the theological role or function the Messiah fulfills.</note>.

LXV. First, therefore, a passage presents itself to me: *Zechariah chapter 9, verse 9: "Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion: behold, your King comes to you; he is righteous and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon a donkey, and upon a colt, the foal of a donkey."* <note>original Latin: "lætare, filia Sion: ecce Rex tuus venit tibi justus, Servator, pauper, insidens asino, & pullo asinæ"</note> *Matthew chapter 21, verse 5* interprets these words as referring to the Messiah. ->## JUDAICA ##<-

"These are the generations of Perez," etc. <note>Ruth 4:18</note> and so forth. And for what reason are these written "defectively"? <note>original Hebrew: חסרין (chaserin). This refers to the word *Toledoth* being spelled without the letter Vav.</note> It is in opposition to the six things that were taken away from the first Adam, and they are: his radiance, his life, his height, the fruit of the earth, the fruits of the tree, and the luminaries. <note>These "six things" are a common theme in Midrashic literature (e.g., Genesis Rabbah 12:6), representing the perfection lost after the Fall.</note> All of these are destined to return in the days of the King Messiah who comes from Zion; therefore, his "generations" <note>Hebrew: תולדותיו (toledotav)</note> are written "full," <note>Spelled with the letter Vav.</note> for he shall fill the deficiency of the world.

So that these matters may be more rightly understood, certain things must be explained beforehand. The word **Toledoth** <term>Toledoth: A Hebrew word meaning "generations," "descendants," or "histories."</term> is written primarily in three ways. **I.** Entirely **defectively**, so that no *Vav* appears, which they call <gloss>the defective of the defective</gloss> <note>original: חסר דחסר (chaser de-chaser)</note>, that is, extremely defective; for example, *Exodus 6:16: These are the names of the sons of Levi* **according to their generations** <note>original: לתולדתם (spelled without Vavs)</note>. **II.** With the **latter** *Vav* missing, as in *Genesis 5:1: This is the record of the* **generations** <note>original: תולדת (missing the second Vav)</note> *or genealogy of Adam.* **III.** With the **first** *Vav* missing, as in *Genesis 37:2: These are the* **generations** <note>original: תולדות (missing the first Vav)</note> *of Jacob.* Finally, there is a time when the same word is <gloss>full of the full</gloss> <note>original: מלא דמלא (malei de-malei)</note>, or entirely full, but this is rare. Hence the *Masora* <term>Masora: The tradition of notes and rules developed by Jewish scholars to preserve the precise text of the Hebrew Bible.</term> regarding *Genesis 2:4*, where the beginning of the world is discussed—when all things were still "very good"—found the words: *These are the* **generations** <note>original: תולדות (spelled with both Vavs)</note> *or origins of the heavens and the earth,* and left this note: <gloss>two instances are "full of the full,"</gloss> <note>original: ב׳ מל דמל</note> that is, two are written entirely "fully."

# JEWISH MATTERS

That golden trees in the Temple produced fruit in their season, even if it is argued from *Nahum* 1:5, was nevertheless spoken metaphorically. <note>The author is likely referring to legends found in the Talmud (Yoma 21b) describing golden trees in the First Temple that blossomed and bore fruit miraculously.</note>

LXXVIII. The main point is this: what is presented by the Jews should not be accepted immediately just as it sounds. For they are accustomed to concealing and keeping secret, in various ways, the mysteries they received from their ancestors; this is a point frequently emphasized by the celebrated Schickard <note>Wilhelm Schickard (1592–1635), a German polymath and professor of Hebrew and Astronomy.</note> and others. And indeed, in this matter, they measure the dignity of the original state by the height of stature. They claim that as soon as man fell from that state, his stature was diminished, so that it was no more than **one hundred cubits** <note>original Hebrew: מאה אמות (*me'ah amot*). A cubit is an ancient unit of length, roughly the distance from the elbow to the tip of the middle finger.</note>, whereas previously it **reached even to the heavens** <note>original Hebrew: הגיע לשמים (*higi'a lashamayim*)</note>, which is to say, it was supreme. For in the same place in the *Talmud*, they say: **from the earth even to the firmament is a journey of 500 years** <note>original Hebrew: מן הארץ ועד לרקיע מהלך ת"ק שנה (*min ha'aretz v'ad larakia mahalach 500 shanah*). This is a common Talmudic measurement for the vast scale of the cosmos.</note>. Such then was the stature of the first Adam—that is, the *dignity of the first state in which he was created.*

Nor does the language of Scripture diverge from this style. Saul’s stature is praised in *1 Samuel* 10:23, **that he was taller than all the people, not only by his head, but from his shoulders and upwards** <note>original Hebrew: ויגבה מכל העם משכמו ומעלה (*vayigbah mikol ha'am mishichmo vamalah*)</note>; hence his subsequent fall is emphasized by mentioning that same stature in *Chapter 28:20*: **he fell the full length of his stature** <note>original Hebrew: ויפל מלא קומתו (*vayipol melo komato*)</note>, or "he fell as long as he was" <note>original German and Latin: *er fiel / so lang er immer war* / *quantus quantus erat*</note>.

# CABBALA

362.

->CABBALA<-

<meta>catchword: ...pleted,</meta>

The letter *He* is missing <note>original Hebrew: חס' ה'</note> though it is read "and I will be glorified" <note>original Hebrew: וקרי' ואכבד'</note>. Why is it that the letter *He* is missing? These are the things that distinguish the First Temple from the Second Temple. And they are: the Ark, the Mercy Seat and the Cherubim, the Fire, the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>original Hebrew: שכינה; the Divine Presence</note>, the Holy Spirit, and the <term>Urim and Thummim</term> <note>original Hebrew: אורים ותומים; the sacred oracular instruments used by the High Priest</note>. The commentator <note>Scholiastes</note> adds these words: "And I will be glorified" <note>original Hebrew: ואכבד</note> lacks the letter *He*. In the <term>Gemara</term> <note>The component of the Talmud comprising rabbinical analysis</note> regarding the book of Haggai, the Scripture speaks of the Second Temple. The Ark, the Mercy Seat, and the Cherubim are all considered as one single thing. And the *Shekhinah* did not dwell in it. And the Holy Spirit did not dwell in the prophets after the second year of Darius.

The **Early Prophets** [are distinguished] from the divisions of Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi, who are called the **Later Prophets**. From the death of the Later Prophets, the **Holy Spirit** <note>original: רוח הקדש (*Ruach Ha-Kodesh*)—referring here specifically to the cessation of the age of prophecy</note> was withdrawn from Israel, though they still made use of the **Daughter of a Voice** <note>original: בת קול (*Bat Kol*); a divine echo or heavenly voice that served as a lower form of communication from God after direct prophecy ended</note>. Now, from the time the Later Prophets died, the Holy Spirit was taken away from Israel, and until now they used that kind of oracle which is called the **Bat Kol**. LXXXV. **"This"** <note>original Hebrew: *Zot* (זאת)</note> through *Gematria* <term>Gematria: A Kabbalistic system of interpretation that assigns numerical values to Hebrew letters; words with the same total value are thought to be spiritually connected.</term> is equivalent to **"This is for the days of the Messiah,"** <note>original Hebrew: *le-yemot ha-mashiach* (לימות המשיח)</note> and next to it is the phrase **"and He will make you abundant,"** <note>Deuteronomy 30:9</note> meaning that if you return in repentance, forgiveness will immediately flow like a river. Nor do they [the Jews] flee to the concept of repentance without cause; it is upon this repentance that they, even today, make the arrival of the Messiah depend, and they seek by every means to find a way to escape the force of our arguments. This suggests that because Phinehas acted with a specific "measure" of zeal, he received an equal measure of reward.</note> **"My covenant of peace": "Peace"** <gloss>Hebrew: *shalom*</gloss> **is written with a "broken vav"** <gloss>Hebrew: *vav keti'ah*</gloss> **because Phinehas is actually Elijah.** <note>Jewish tradition often identifies the zealot Phinehas with the prophet Elijah, suggesting they share the same soul or that Phinehas never truly died.</note> **And so, "Elijah"** <gloss>Hebrew: *Eliyah*</gloss> **is written lacking the vav, while "Jacob"** <gloss>Hebrew: *Ya'akov*</gloss> **is written in full with a vav; for Jacob took the vav from Elijah as a pledge until he comes with the Messiah and restores it to his children. And this is what is read in Psalm 14 and Psalm 53: "Let Jacob exult and Israel be glad." The word "shall be glad"** <gloss>Hebrew: *yismach*</gloss> **contains the same letters as "Messiah"** <gloss>Hebrew: *mashiach*</gloss>, **signifying that he will be glad in the days of the Messiah, and he will bring back or restore...**

*Therefore, that is, the word* **laken** *in Gematria has the same value as the words* **midah achat**, (*meaning that because Phinehas had used Zeal,* **laken** *is the reason his priesthood is confirmed by an equal measure.) And as it is said,* **my covenant of peace**, *it is written with a shortened vav in the word* **shalom**; *for Phinehas is Elijah himself (regarding this, see Selden in his "Treatise on Succession," p. 232), whence also, with the vav missing, it is written* **Eliyah** *in Malachi 4:5; but* **Ya'akov** *is written fully with the vav: for he took the vav from Elijah as a pledge, until he comes with the Messiah and liberates his children. And this is what is read in Psalms 14 and 53, the final verse: "Let Jacob exult and"* **yismach**, *"Israel be glad." Truly* **yismach** *has the same letters as* **Mashiach** <note>The letters are Yud-Shin-Mem-Chet (yismach) and Mem-Shin-Yud-Chet (mashiach).</note>, *so that he may rejoice in the days of the Messiah, and bring back or restore...*

Two things are to be noted here: One is that among the good Angels, opinions regarding mortal affairs vary; hence, in **Daniel 10:13**, the *Angel prince of the kingdom of the Persians is read to have resisted another for twenty-one days, until Michael, one of the chief princes, came to his aid.* 

The second point is that in the **Talmud**, Tractate **Sanhedrin**, chapter 4, a certain **Senate of Angels** is introduced with these words: <note>original Hebrew/Aramaic: אין הקב"ה עושה דבר אלא אם כן נמלך בפמליא של מעלה שנאמר בגזירת עירין פתגמא ובמימר קדישין שאלתא (*Ein Ha-Kadosh Baruch Hu oseh davar ela im ken nimlach be-familia shel ma’alah...*)</note> that is: *The Holy One, Blessed be He, does nothing unless He has first taken counsel with the family above (the Angels), because it is said in Daniel 4:17 <note>The source cites Dan. 4:14 following the Latin Vulgate numbering</note>, "The matter is by the decree of the watchers, and the demand by the word of the Holy Ones."*

**Ludovicus de Dieu** <note>a prominent 17th-century Dutch Orientalist and linguist</note>, in his *Notes on the Acts of the Apostles*, assembled a kind of Angelic Senate from this passage, and I am surprised that others have followed him; certainly, that opinion comes very close to the views of the Jews. 

See also **Rabbi Solomon Jarchi** <note>commonly known as Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval Jewish commentator</note> on **Genesis 1:26**, where he refers the word **"let us make"** <note>original Hebrew: נעשה (*na’aseh*)</note> to the Angels, <note>original Hebrew: אעפ שלא סייעוהו ביצירתו (*af al pi she-lo siye’uhu be-yetzirato*)</note> that is: *even though they were not His assistants in the creation.* 

The arguments that theologians dispute against him and the **Photinians** <note>a Christian sect following Photinus of Sirmium, who denied the Trinity and the pre-existence of Christ, arguing that the "us" in Genesis did not refer to the Trinity</note> are well known even to the general public, and can be sought from **Jacobus Martinus** <note>a Lutheran philosopher and theologian (1570–1649)</note> in the first book of *On the Trinity of the Elohim*. See also **Pineda**, Volume 1 <note>Juan de Pineda (1558–1637), a Spanish Jesuit scholar known for his extensive commentaries</note>.

**105.** Furthermore, it is said in **Exodus 23:23**, *My Angel* <note>Hebrew: מלאכי (*mal’achi*)</note> *shall go before you*: opinions vary among the commentators as to how this should be understood. There were those who asserted that by "Angel" <note>Hebrew: מלאך (*mal’ach*)</note>, the **book of the Law** <term>the Torah, or the first five books of the Bible</term> is understood, a reasoning deduced from the words *for my name is in him* <note>Hebrew: כי שמי בקרבו (*ki shemi be-kirbo*)</note>; for the name of someone is much more correctly said to be in a book than in a person. Others referred it to the **Ark of the Covenant** <note>Hebrew: ארון הברית (*aron ha-berit*)</note>. 

But **Aben-Ezra** <note>Abraham ibn Ezra (1089–1167), a celebrated Spanish rabbi, philosopher, and biblical exegete known for his grammatical approach</note> responds vigorously: *All these words are wind* <note>Hebrew: וכל דברי רוח (*ve-chol divrei ruach*), an idiom meaning the arguments are empty or vain</note>, since mention of Angels sent by God is made so often, especially in **Daniel**, where Michael is called *your prince* <note>Hebrew: מיכאל שרכם (*Michael sarechem*)</note>—namely, the prince of the Jews—in **Daniel 10:21**. And in verse 13 of the same chapter, he is called *one of the chief princes* <note>Hebrew: אחד השרים הראשונים (*achad ha-sarim ha-rishonim*)</note>, or an **Archangel** <note>Greek: ἀρχάγγελος (*archangelos*)</note> as in the **Epistle of Jude, verse 9**. From this he concludes: *This angel is Michael himself, called the prince of the Jews* <note>Hebrew: זה המלאך מיכאל (*zeh ha-mal’ach Michael*)</note>. This is surely based on a very pleasing allusion and a very easy transposition of letters <note>In Hebrew, the letters of "My Angel" (M-L-A-K-Y) are an anagram of the name "Michael" (M-Y-K-A-L)</note>. 

Hence, **Baal Hatturim** <note>Jacob ben Asher (c. 1269–1343), a legal scholar and commentator who often employed "Gematria" or numerical and letter-based hints in his work</note>, on **Exodus 32:34** where the same words are repeated, says: *The letters of "My Angel" [are the same as Michael]...*

"My Angel" <note>original: מלאכי (*mal’achi*)</note>, that is to say, the word *Michael*, who is the "My Angel" specifically assigned to him. This name contains the same letters as the word *Michael* <note>original: מיכאל; both names use the Hebrew letters Mem, Lamed, Aleph, Kaph, and Yod</note>, as if to say that Michael is his own personal Angel, or "he is my own and unique Angel."

**106.** I will also add other examples concerning Angels. In **Numbers 22:38**, Balaam says: "I shall speak that which [God] has put *in my mouth*" <note>original: בפי אלהים (*be-fi Elohim*)</note>. This means the word "in my mouth" <note>original: בפי (*be-fi*)</note> numerically coincides with the word "Angel" <note>original: מלאך (*mal’ach*)</note> through **Gematria** <term>a system where Hebrew letters are assigned numerical values to find hidden connections between words</term>. By the same branch of the Cabbala, it also coincides with "The Name" <note>original: השם (*HaShem*), a common title for God</note>, because the Angel called *Elohim* <note>a name for God often interpreted by mystics as a divine messenger or power</note> gave him that decree or placed it in his mouth, which he was then required to speak back to Balak. Thus, they understand this to refer to a created Angel. 

In **Numbers 8:4**, regarding the construction of the lampstand <note>the Menorah</note>, it says: "according to the pattern" <note>original: כמראה (*ke-mareh*)</note> "which the Lord had shown to Moses." Here, they write again: *The word "according to the pattern" is, by Gematria, the same as "like Gabriel," which teaches that Gabriel showed him the form of the lampstand, and he made it accordingly* <note>original: כמראה בגימטריא כגבריאל מלמד שגבריאל הראה לו דמות המנורה כן עשה</note>. This means the word "according to the pattern" <note>original: כמראה</note> is numerically identical to "like Gabriel" <note>original: כגבריאל</note>, showing that the Archangel Gabriel acted as the divine architect or instructor for Moses.

He indeed calls himself the "strong man" <note>original Hebrew: *Geber* (גבר); in biblical Hebrew this means a man or a warrior, but in Rabbinic Hebrew, it can also mean a rooster</note>, *Numbers 24:3*. It is a solemn custom among the Jews to play with the various meanings of words; for this reason, the very expression in *Isaiah 22:17* was rendered as "rooster" <note>original Latin: *gallum gallinaceum*</note> by the teacher of **Jerome**, just as the **Holy Father** <note>Saint Jerome (c. 347–420 AD), the translator of the Vulgate Bible, who studied with Jewish scholars to understand the Hebrew text</note> himself handed down in his *Commentary* on that passage. In the book *The Chronicles of Moses*, similar things are recounted concerning Balaam and his sons.

...Balaam is like a rooster <note>original Latin: *gallo gallinaceo*</note>. **120.** Thus the enemy <note>Balaam, who is traditionally viewed as an archetypal enemy of Israel in Jewish thought</note> seemed sufficiently harassed, unless some defense remained from the **Kabbalah** <term>Kabbalah: The ancient Jewish tradition of mystical interpretation of the Bible</term>. For the text says in *Numbers 22:30*: *And the donkey said to Balaam: "Am I not your donkey, on whom you have ridden <note>original Hebrew: *rakavta alai* (רכבת עלי)</note> so long until this day?"* Indeed, through the method of **Gematria** <term>Gematria: A system where Hebrew letters represent numbers, allowing for hidden connections to be found between words of equal value</term>, this phrase "on whom you have ridden" coincides with the word "you have copulated with me" <note>original Hebrew: *ribatani* (רבעתני)</note>, implying he had mated with the animal for a long time. Likewise, in *Numbers 23:10*, Balaam speaks thus: *Let my soul die the death of the upright, and let my end be like his.* Regarding these words, the Kabbalah remarks the following:

In the **Masorah** <term>Masorah: A collection of grammatical and linguistic notes on the Hebrew Bible meant to preserve the text</term>, the phrase "Let my soul die the death of the upright" appears three times. The word "death" is also written three times in a manner suggesting "Let my soul die with the Philistines" <note>referencing Judges 16:30, the death of Samson</note> and elsewhere, "Their soul dies in youth" <note>referencing Job 36:14</note>. He [Balaam] sought for his soul to "die with the upright," but it was not so. On the contrary, he died the death of the Philistines—that is, the death of the wicked—and in his youth. Truly, men of blood and deceit do not live out half their days <note>referencing Psalm 55:23</note>, for he was only thirty-seven years old when **Phinehas** <note>The grandson of Aaron the priest, who executed judgment in the wilderness</note> killed him. The word "Upright" <note>original Hebrew: *Yesharim* (ישרים)</note> has the same numerical value in Gematria as "The Tablets of the World" <note>original Hebrew: *Luchot ha-Olam* (לכות העולם). The author suggests a mystical equivalence between the fate of the righteous and the fundamental laws of the universe</note>.

The final letters of the names of the Patriarchs are equal in Gematria <term>Gematria: A Kabbalistic method where Hebrew letters are assigned numerical values to find hidden meanings</term> to the name "Balaam," and this is the meaning of the phrase "and let my end be like his." <note>This refers to Numbers 23:10. This is the meaning of what he says: "and let my end be like his," or like those fathers, by swapping the numbers. 

But he "returned to his place" <note>original Hebrew: *shav li-mekomo* (שב למקומו)</note>, that is, he descended into **Gehenna** <term>Gehenna: A place of spiritual punishment or purification in Jewish thought</term>, as recorded by the same **Baal Ha-Turim** <note>Rabbi Jacob ben Asher, a 14th-century commentator famous for his Gematria-based insights</note> at the end of *Numbers 24*. Regarding the initial and final letters in the names of the Patriarchs, there is another Kabbalistic tradition in Baal Ha-Turim regarding *Exodus 6:3*.

Concerning the Judges, the Enemies, the Priesthood, and the economic state, nearly innumerable examples occur. I would like to bring a few of them into the open. Regarding the **selection of a King**, the following is held in *Deuteronomy 17:14-15: When you have entered the land... and said, "I will set a king over me, like all the nations around me": you shall set over you him whom the Lord has chosen from among your brothers.* In the Hebrew, it is said "from among your brothers" <note>original Hebrew: *mi-kerev acheicha* (מקרב אחיך)</note>, which words coincide through **Gematria** <term>Gematria: A system where Hebrew letters represent numbers, revealing connections between words with the same total value</term> with the phrase "from the tribe of Judah" <note>original Hebrew: *shevet yehudah* (שבט יהודה)</note>. Indeed, Saul was not from that tribe, but David was. And in verse 20, it <note>the text or perhaps a specific phrase within the law of the King</note> **begins with Lamed and ends in Lamed** <note>Lamed is the Hebrew letter 'L'</note>. In the system of numbers, Lamed is worth 30. And so, "he was 30 years old when he began to reign" <note>original Hebrew: *ben lamed shanah be-malko* (בן ל' שנה במלכו)</note> is hinted at regarding David. In the same place, it is said, "so that he may prolong his days" <note>original Hebrew: *le-ma'an ya'arik yamim* (למען יאריך ימים)</note>, namely: **That king will prolong his days in his kingdom who reigned having been born thirty years earlier, but not Saul.** <note>The author is using the numerical value of the letter Lamed (30) to argue that the biblical text subtly predestined David, who was 30 when crowned, for a long reign, while Saul was excluded from this promise.</note>

CXXII. Concerning the **Judges**, in *Exodus 21:1*, they have an excellent Kabbalistic interpretation. The words of the Scripture are: *These are the judgments which you shall set before them* <note>original Hebrew: *ve-eleh ha-mishpatim asher tasim lifnehem* (וְאֵלֶה הַמִּשְׁפָּטִים אֲשֶׁר תָּשִׂים לִפְנֵיהֶם)</note>. From here, several rules emerge, chiefly by this method: **Notarikon** <term>Notarikon: A Kabbalistic method using the first or last letters of words to form new words or acronyms, often to derive legal or mystical maxims</term>. [The first words imply:] "A man is obligated to investigate the law" <note>original Hebrew: *v'chayav adam lachkor ha-din* (וחייב אדם לחקור הדין)</note> based on the verse; and by Notarikon: "The judge is commanded to perform an act of compromise in the order of the ruling" <note>original Hebrew: *ha-dayan mitzaveh ma'aseh pesharah seder pesak* (הדיין מצווה מעשה פשרה סדר פסק)</note>.

# JUDAICA

And now for the judgment: The word *L'mar* <note>original: למר</note> is a **Notarikon** <term>Notarikon: A Kabbalistic method of interpretation where the letters of a single word are treated as an acronym for a whole phrase</term> for "to hear both sides" <note>original: לס סניהס</note>; *Ruus* <note>original: רווס</note> and *Chatus* <note>original: חטוס</note> <unclear>illegible abbreviations</unclear> indicate the **Notarikon** "you shall hear both of them speaking together"; and "before them" <note>original: לפניהם</note> is a **Notarikon** for "do not favor the face of the noble, and the honor [of the status] should be hidden from them."

The meaning is this: the word **And these** <note>original Hebrew: *Ve-eleh* (ואלה), from Exodus 21:1</note> through **Notarikon**, a species of **Kabbalah** <term>Kabbalah: A tradition of Jewish mysticism that seeks hidden meanings in the biblical text</term>, signifies that a man (specifically a Judge) is bound to search out what is just. The second word, **the judgments** <note>original Hebrew: *Ha-mishpatim* (המשפטים)</note>, through that same Kabbalistic method, implies that it is commanded to the judge that he properly explain the matter before he brings forth a verdict. 

The third word, **which** <note>original Hebrew: *Asher* (אשר)</note>, through the same Notarikon, requires that there be the consent of both parties. The fourth word, **you shall set** <note>original Hebrew: *Tashim* (תשים)</note>, by the same art, notes that both the defendant and the plaintiff must be heard speaking about the case together in person. The fifth word, **before them** <note>original Hebrew: *Lifneichem* (לפניהם)</note>, implies through that same artifice that the external face of a magnificent man should not be so attended to in judgment that the judge pretends to be someone else for that person's sake—in the same manner that Joseph behaved <note>Joseph initially feigned being a stranger to his brothers</note> in **Genesis 42:7**.

CXXIII. Just as these observations must be noted by a judge, so too, as the occasion arises, we should relate what the **Rabbis** <term>Rabbis: Jewish scholars and teachers of the law</term> pass down concerning the throne of Solomon, which they claim is derived from the **Kabbalah** of their ancestors. The words of Scripture in **1 Kings 10:18-20** are: *King Solomon made a great throne of ivory and overlaid it with the finest gold. The throne had* **SIX STEPS**, *and two lions stood at the armrests, etc. Nothing like it had ever been made in any kingdom.*

### CXXIV. Their opinion is as follows:

Come and see. Solomon’s throne had six steps. From where is this established? From the First Book of Kings, chapter 10. And in this Mosaic section <note>the portion of the Torah written by Moses</note> titled *Shoftim*, six prohibitions are contained as a place of confirmation, namely these: you shall not pervert justice, you shall not show partiality, nor shall you accept a gift, or plant a grove, or erect a statue, or offer to the Lord your God anything in which there is a blemish. Behold, six emerge. A certain herald, moreover, stood before the throne of Solomon, shouting to the King as he ascended the first step: "Beware you do not pervert justice"; at the second: "Be a stranger to the showing of partiality"; at the third: "You shall not accept a gift"; at the fourth: "You shall not plant a grove for yourself"; at the fifth: "Neither shall you erect a statue"; at the sixth: "You shall not sacrifice to the Lord your God anything in which there is a blemish." The same things are repeated in *Ir Gibborim* <note>original: עיר גבורים; "City of Mighty Men," a homiletic commentary by Solomon Ephraim Luntschitz</note>, number 45.

### CXXVI.

But I am wandering further than I had intended. I said that the Kabbalists <term>Kabbalists: Practitioners of Jewish mysticism who seek to understand the hidden nature of God and the universe</term> themselves compare the terms *Dayan* <note>original: דיין; "Judge"</note> and *Elohim*. For they believe that the name *YHWH* [יהוה] <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God</note> signifies mercy [רחמים], while the name *Elohim* [אלהים] signifies the attribute of judgment [מדת]. He repeats these same points on Exodus 22.

### CXXVII.

**Exodus 15:18.** Moses, in the Song <note>The Song of the Sea, sung by the Israelites after crossing the Red Sea</note>, speaks thus with the Israelites: יְהוָה יִמְלֹךְ לְעֹלָם וָעֶד, *The Lord shall reign forever and ever.* Concerning the **Pesik** <term>Pesik: A vertical line (|) used as a musical or liturgical accent in the Hebrew Bible to indicate a distinct pause between words</term>, which is placed between two words, they say the following: "The Lord shall reign"—there is a pause to tell you that when the time comes when they shall say, "The Lord reigns, the Lord reigned, the Lord shall reign forever and ever," the kingdom of the Lord shall never cease. And the Holy One, blessed be He, tested the kingdom, and the generation of the Holy One, blessed be He, shall reign; "the Lord shall reign forever and ever." There is a **Pesik** nearby because *the way of the wicked He subverts* <note>Psalm 146:9</note>. He did not want to mention the Divine Name immediately following the "wicked." That is, *The Lord shall reign*: here is the accent **Pesik**, to indicate to you that when the time comes when they will say, *The Lord reigns, the Lord reigns* (as in **Micah 4:7**), truly the Lord will reign for the age and beyond, and thus the kingdom of the worldly nations shall then cease.

In this way, Moses in this passage placed the Name of God before the word for "reigning," whereas David placed it after, saying in **Psalm 146:10**, *The Lord shall reign forever*; because the immediately preceding verse ended with these words: *He subverts the way of the WICKED*, he did not want to immediately join the Name of Go... <note>The text likely continues to explain that David delayed the Name of God to keep it separate from the mention of the "wicked" in the prior verse</note>

# JUDAICA

...or to connect that [name] to wickedness. ### CXXVIII.

Naturally, therefore, they are very hostile toward the <note>original: אומות העולם; *Umot HaOlam*</note> *nations of the world*, while they flatter themselves. There is a common saying among them, noted by the **Baal HaTurim** <note>The author uses the abbreviation ב"ה (*B.H.*) as a shorthand for this source hereafter</note> on **Leviticus 24**: <note>original: כל הסטור לועו של ישראל כאילו סוטר לועה של שכינה; *Kol ha-soter lo’o shel Yisrael k’ilu soter lo’ah shel Shekhinah*</note> *whoever strikes a Jew on the cheek, it is as if he strikes the cheek of the Divine Presence itself*; this is taken from the **Talmud**, tractate **Sanhedrin**, chapter 7, where it is attributed to a certain **Rabbi Chanina**, who proves it from **Proverbs 20:25**. Regarding others, however, they say on **Exodus 9:20**: <note>original: טוב שבגוים הרוג; *Tov she-ba-goyim harog*</note> *the best of the Gentiles should be killed*, and even <note>original: טוב שברופאים לגיהנם; *Tov she-ba-rofe'im l'Gehenna*</note> *the best of physicians is worthy of Gehenna* <note>The author likely refers to a famous Mishnaic adage (Kiddushin 4:14) regarding the fallibility or arrogance of doctors</note>. They also say elsewhere: <note>original: טוב שבנחשים רצוץ; *Tov she-ba-nachashim retzotz*</note> *the best of snakes—crush its head*. Thus, it was enough for **Rabbi Solomon** <note>Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval French rabbi and commentator</note> to write on **Genesis 15:9–10**: *Because the nations are compared to bulls, rams, and goats, as it is said, "Many bulls have surrounded me," etc.*

# CABBALA

<note>original Hebrew: חסר להיות בעל הקרנים וזכר פרס וחלק הצפור מלך יון . וישראל נמשלו לבני יונה כ' יונתי בחגוי לפיכך בתר הבהמות רמז מיהו האומות כלין וזה הצפור לא בתר רמז מיהו וישראל קיימין לעולם</note>
...was lacking, being the "master of horns," the ram of Persia, and the portion of the bird [representing] the King of Greece. Israel, however, is compared to the young of a dove, as it is written: *My dove, in the clefts of the rock* <note>Song of Solomon 2:14</note>. Therefore, by dividing the animals, he hinted that the nations would perish; but because he did not divide the bird, he hinted that Israel shall endure forever.

That is to say: because the nations of the world are compared to bullocks, rams, and goats (as is established in **Psalm 22:13**, *bulls have surrounded me*, and the **Prophecy of Daniel 8:20**, *the ram which you saw having horns represents the kings of Media and Persia*, and **v. 21**, *the shaggy goat is the King of Greece*), the Jews are compared to the young of a dove, according to that passage in **Song of Solomon 2:14**, *my dove in the clefts of the rock*. Furthermore, the division of those [other] animals signifies that their identity and existence will be consumed. But that which follows—that the bird was not divided—indicates that the Jews will remain forever.

### CXXIX.
Indeed, they explain their thinking more fully in various places, especially against the **Roman Kingdom** and its faith. For that kingdom itself is called <note>original: מלכות חייבת; *Malchut Chayevet*</note> the **Guilty Kingdom**, or <note>original: אדום הערלים; *Edom Ha-Arelim*</note> **Uncircumcised Edom** <note>In medieval Jewish literature, "Edom" became a standard code-word for the Roman Empire and, by extension, the Christian Church</note>. Christ is called <note>original: מלכות הרשעה; *Malchut ha-Rish’ah*</note> the **Wicked Kingdom** and the **Wicked Edom**. His Gospel is called <note>original: און גליון; *Aven Gilyon*</note> the **Scroll of Iniquity** <note>A derogatory Hebrew pun on the Greek word *Euangelion* (Gospel). While *Euangelion* means "Good News," *Aven Gilyon* means "Empty/Sinful Scroll"</note>. Likewise, his law is called <note>original: תורת ערלים; *Torat Arelim*</note> the **Law of the Uncircumcised**. The one who presides over this office is called <note>original: שר נמרוד; *Sar Nimrod*</note> **Prince Nimrod**, or <note>original: רשע בן רשע; *Resha ben Resha*</note> **Wicked son of a wicked man**, etc. In the **Sefer ha-Gilgulim** <term>Sefer ha-Gilgulim: "The Book of Reincarnations," a Kabbalistic work primarily associated with the teachings of Isaac Luria</term>, the following appears regarding chapter 6:

<note>original Hebrew: והלכתי וגליתי ולקחתי ארבעה לשונות של כנגד ארבע מלכויות . ובאחרון כתיב כנגד אדום ועל כן כתיב ביה ולקחתי כהדין הלוקח בחזקה</note>
*I went and I revealed and I took four tongues corresponding to the four kingdoms. And in the last one, it is written regarding Edom; therefore, it is written regarding it "and I took," like one who takes by force.*

<note>original Hebrew: חילו וכלם קמה סחיט</note> *His strength and all of them stood up as aftergrowth.* That is, in the ninth and tenth verses <note>likely referring to the Song of the Sea in Exodus 15</note>, four specific words are read: <note>original: הוסיף, הציל, נחל, לקח; hosif, hitzil, nachal, lakach</note> *added*, *delivered*, *inherited*, and *took*. These terms are used in the context of liberation and are seen to correspond to the "four kingdoms" of biblical prophecy. It is notable that in the final position, the word **"took"** is used; this is referred to the **Kingdom of the Edomites**—which is to say, the **Romans**. This word is chosen to compare their method of "liberating" or taking territory to a man who violently extorts or snatches something away from another. For that fourth kingdom surpasses all others in its sheer strength and violence.

### CXXX.
In **Leviticus 26:5**, a passage where they believe the hope for their ultimate liberation is most firmly rooted, we read: *You shall eat your bread* <note>original: לשובע; le-sova</note> **to satiety**, *and you shall dwell securely in your land: and I will grant* <note>original: שלום; shalom</note> **peace** *in the land; you shall sleep, and there shall be none to make you afraid; I will remove* <note>original: חיה רעה; chayah ra’ah</note> **evil beasts** *from the land, so that the sword shall not pass through your land.* The Jewish gloss on *this* <note>original: זה</note> is as follows:

<note>original Hebrew: לשובע בגימטריא אפילו אוכל קמעא קיימת • שלום אותיות לשמו • ממנו שלום • והסבתי חיה רעה בגימטריא אלו ד' מלכויות בבל מדי יון אדום</note>

That is: what is said regarding **"to satiety"** signifies through <term>Gematria|A traditional Jewish system of assigning numerical values to Hebrew letters to derive deeper meanings</term> that *even if one eats only a little, they shall be sustained.* Within the word **"peace"** (*Shalom*) lies the hidden phrase **"for His name"** (*Lishmo*), because the name of the <term>Messiah|The promised redeemer of the Jewish people</term> (according to **Isaiah 9:6**) *shall be Peace.* Furthermore, the words **"I will remove evil beasts"** signify, through Gematria, the four kingdoms: **Babylonia**, the **Medes**, the **Greeks**, and the **Edomites** (the **Romans**). This interpretation alludes to the symbolic animals described in the **Book of Daniel**.

# CABBALA

Daniel 8, as stated in thesis 128. [Martinus Becanus in his *Manual*, book 1, chapter 5, section 66, notes that <note>original Hebrew: חיתו שדי; chayto shadai</note> **"the beasts of the field"** mentioned in Isaiah 56:9 are the **ROMANS**, so called "beasts of the field" on account of their faithlessness. ### CXXXI.
Saint Jerome is the authority for the fact that the Jews once interpreted many things as referring to the Romans. For example, regarding **Isaiah 34**, he says: *The Hebrews contend that these things were prophesied concerning the Roman Empire; and that the devastation of a once most powerful kingdom is foretold as vengeance for Zion.* He says the same regarding chapter 26, where it is written: *He shall bring down the inhabitants of* <note>original Hebrew: מרום; marom</note> **the heights**, *he shall humble the lofty city: as the Jews think, this is **ROME**, though we believe it is more correctly proven to be Jerusalem, etc.* And on **Joel 1**, where it is said: *what the palmerworm left, the locust has eaten; and what the locust left, the cankerworm has eaten; and what the cankerworm left, the blight <note>or caterpillar</note> has eaten;* he writes as follows: *The Hebrews interpret the 'palmerworm' as the Assyrians, Babylonians, and Chaldeans; the 'locust' as the Medes and Persians; the 'cankerworm' as the Macedonians and all the successors of Alexander; and they refer the 'blight' to the Roman Empire, who, as the fourth and last, oppressed the Jews so greatly that they drove them from their own borders.* Regarding **Joel 3:19**: *Idumæa <note>Edom</note> shall be a wilderness of destruction.* In

This world and the world to come were created because it is said in Isaiah 26:4: "God through the particles *Tsur*," that is, *Tsayyer* (He fashioned). The **Cabbalistic** <term>Cabbalistic: relating to Kabbalah, Jewish mystical interpretation</term> sense here is: *be-He bera'am*, that is, "He created them through the letter **He**" (treating the letter **He** as the material cause). Therefore, say that this world was founded through **He**, and the future world through **Yod**. What is the reason for the letter **He**? While it points downward, it is interrupted; thus, it indicates to all coming into the world (Isaiah 57:9) that they shall descend into **Sheol**. <note>The shape of the letter He (ה) has a large opening at the bottom, symbolizing the "wide gate" of death, but a small opening at the top left, symbolizing the narrow way of repentance and return to God.</note>

# ->CABBALA<-

Seven crowns <note>original: "tagin" (ז׳ תגין); these are decorative flourishes or "thorns" added to the tops of specific letters in a Torah scroll</note> correspond to the seven names for the Evil Inclination <note>original: "Yetzer Hara" (יצר הרע), the innate human impulse toward selfishness or sin</note>; and seven levels of Hell. 

*That is, the letter* Shin [ש] *in the word* "Tissa" <note>original: "tissa" (תשא) from Exodus 30:12, "When you take [a census]"</note> *has seven points <note>referring to the decorative "crowns" on the letter's branches</note> which refer to the seven names of the evil inclination and the seven levels of hell. Specifically, it is written in the Talmud, in the Tractate* Sukkah: The Holy One, blessed be He, called the Evil Inclination "Evil"; Moses called it "Uncircumcision"; David called it "Unclean"; Solomon called it "Enemy"; Isaiah called it "Stumbling-block"; Ezekiel called it "Stone"; Joel called it "The Hidden One" <note>original: "Tzefoni" (צפוני), which can mean "the northern one" or "the hidden/lurking one"</note>. 

*This means the Evil Inclination has seven names. God, the Holy One (blessed be He), calls it* Evil, *in Genesis 8:21. Moses calls it* uncircumcision <note>original: "orlah" (ערלה)</note>, *in Deuteronomy 10:16. David calls it* unclean *—which is inferred from Psalm 51:10 where he asks for a* clean *heart. Solomon calls it* enemy, *in Proverbs 25:21. Isaiah calls it* a stumbling-block, *in chapter 57. Ezekiel calls it* a stone, *in chapter 36:26. Joel calls it* the hidden one, *in chapter 2:20.* 

*These names are discussed at length in* The City of Heroes <note>original: "Ir Gibborim" (עיר גבורים), a 16th-century homiletic work by Solomon Ephraim Luntschitz</note>, *specifically in the section "Circumcise the Four Identities," and it is said there: that the serpent cast into Eve four impurities from the four spirits of uncleanness: the spirit of folly, the spirit of fornication, the spirit of evil desire, etc.* 

*Elsewhere, regarding the double inclination of man, this Kabbalistic teaching appears in the* Zohar <note>original: "S'H" (ס׳ה) referring to Sefer Ha-Zohar</note> *regarding Chapter 1 of Genesis:* "And the Lord God formed" <note>Genesis 2:7</note>; *one is written missing a letter, and one is written full. Man is described with the "full" spelling because he has two inclinations: the Good Inclination and the Evil Inclination. But the word "formed" regarding the beasts of the field is "missing" a letter, because they have only one inclination.* 

*That is, the word* Vayyitzer <note>original: "וייצר" (and He formed)</note> *appears twice; once in the full form...* <note>In Genesis 2:7, the word for "formed" regarding man is spelled with two Yods (וייצר), which Kabbalists interpret as representing two "yetzers" or inclinations. In Genesis 2:19, regarding animals, it is spelled with one Yod (ויצר), suggesting a single nature.</note>

The letter **Yod** <note>the tenth and smallest letter of the Hebrew alphabet, often associated with the divine spark</note>, which is again *written defectively without the second Yod.*

For when it is written in Genesis 2:7, "And the Lord God formed [וייצר] man," the *Yod is written in full* <note>using two Yods</note> *because a double inclination falls upon man* (this refers to the word *yetzer* <note>meaning "inclination" or "urge"</note> *beginning with a Yod*): *both the good and the evil.* But in Genesis 2:19, it is *written defectively* as "And the Lord God formed [ויצר] from the ground every beast of the field," *since that double inclination does not fall upon those beasts.* This Kabbalistic interpretation hints—to add this in passing—that God created the "Evil Inclination" <note>original: "Yetzer Hara" (יצר הרע)</note> just as I have shown elsewhere that they themselves establish in the commentary on *Lipmann* <note>referring to Yom-Tov Lipmann-Muhlhausen, a 14th-century polemicist and author of the Sefer HaNitzachon; page 648, number 93</note>.

CXXXIX. Regarding the names of *Gehenna* <note>the place of spiritual purification or punishment</note>, they record these traditions in the Talmud, Tractate *Eruvin*, chapter 2: "Gehenna has seven names: *Sheol*, *Abaddon*, *Beer Shachat*, *Shucha*, *Guy Tzalmavet*, *Charon*, and *Tachtit*." <note>In order, these names translate to: The Underworld, Destruction, Pit of Corruption, The Ditch, Valley of the Shadow of Death, Burning Anger, and The Lowest Depths</note>. A mandate of God also begins with the word **Wine**, <note>original: יין (*Yayin*)</note> from which the following is added: **No verse begins with the word "Wine" except this one, which brought wailing into the world, to show how many were drunk on wine and therefore died.** <note>original: אין פסוק מתחיל יין אלא זה להוכיח יללה בעולם כמה שתוי יין היו ולכך מתו</note> This alludes to another <term>Kabbala</term> <note>In this context, a mystical tradition or interpretation.</note>; for **"Wine" by Gematria is "Wailing,"** <note>original: יין בגימטריא יללה (*Yayin be-gematria yelalah*); Gematria is a system where letters have numerical values. Both "Wine" (Y-Y-N) and "Wailing" (Y-L-L-H) sum to 70 in this tradition.</note> which agrees with the one who said: **The sons of Aaron were inebriated with wine, and for that reason they died.**

**CXLV.** Now, regarding what is said of Aaron's sons, that they consumed wine **by way of drunkenness** <note>original: דרך שכרות (*derech shichrut*)</note> so that they were rendered intoxicated, they again imply this through Kabbalistic analysis. In verse 1, the word **them** <note>original: אתם (*otam*)</note> is written "defectively" <note>Without the letter *vav*.</note>, and in verse 2, the word **them** <note>original: אותם (*otam*)</note> is written "fully" <note>With the letter *vav*.</note>, from which this observation emerges: **The word "them" is written fully with a *vav*, which letter in numbers is worth six. For they committed six sins: They brought strange fire; they gave legal rulings in the presence of their Master** <note>Moses</note>; **they were drunk on wine; they had no children; they set their eyes on positions of leadership; and they did not take counsel.** <note>original: אותם מלא ויו סמכתו בשש דברים . אש זרה . הורו בפני רבם . שתוי יין . בנים לא היו להם . נתנו עיניהם בפרנסות . לא נטלו עצה :</note> That is to say, the word **them** was written fully with the letter *vav*, which stands for the number six. For they admitted six sins. They brought strange fire; they taught in the presence of their Master...

# CABBALA

...of their masters: <note>Continuing from the previous page, this refers to Nadab and Abihu disrespecting their teachers, Moses and Aaron.</note> they were drunk with wine; they fathered no children; they cast their eyes upon the government <note>original: gubernatio; likely referring to their ambition for leadership.</note> and thus did not take counsel from others. Regarding this, in the <term>Talmud</term> <note>The central text of Rabbinic Judaism.</note>, <term>Massechet</term> <note>A "Tractate" or volume of the Talmud.</note> **Sanhedrin**, chapter 4, they noted another disadvantage of wine in these words: **"When wine enters, a secret goes out"** <note>original: נכנס יין יצא סוד (*Nichnas yayin yatza sod*)</note>. The phrase **"Wine enters"** in numbers is equal to 70; and so also is **"A secret goes out."** <note>This is a demonstration of <term>Gematria</term>, where the Hebrew letters for "Wine" (Y-Y-N) and "Secret" (S-W-D) both sum to 70. The text suggests that wine physically displaces wisdom or secrets.</note> Hence, while the wine enters, the **secret** or mystery departs.

**CXLVI.** Furthermore, in the **Jerusalem Talmud**, <term>Massechet</term> **Yoma**, there exists a saying that is harsh to hear, <note>original: durum est auditu; implying a difficult or controversial theological point.</note> in these words: **"The atonement of Manasseh—there was no atonement for him, yet it is written for him: this atonement is the death of the High Priest, as it is said, 'and he shall dwell in it until the death of the High Priest.'"** <note>original: כפרת מנשה לא היה לו כפרה וכתיב לו כפרה זו מיתתו של כהן גדול שנ' וישב בה עד מות כהן הגדול</note> That is to say, for one who kills a person through imprudence or against his will, <note>An accidental killer or manslayer.</note> no expiation was prescribed by Moses, except that which the law almost intimates: that it is the death of the High Priest. As it is said in **Numbers 35:25**, *he shall remain in it* <note>The City of Refuge.</note> *until the High Priest dies.* Does the death of the High Priest really atone for the sins of others? Certainly, the Jews say in the <term>Glossa</term> <note>A commentary or marginal note.</note>: **"This matter appears..."** <note>original: יראה ענין זה (*Yiraeh inyan zeh*)</note>, that is, it seems to be a very foreign thing, since it is **widely known** <note>original: מפורסמות (*Mefursamot*)</note> that each person dies for his own sin. However, because the mention of death is explicit in **the Torah** <note>original: והתורה (*Ve-ha-Torah*)</note>, they therefore say in <term>Massechet</term> **Makkot** of the **Babylonian Talmud**, that the mothers of the priests [provided food] to the man-slayers... <note>The text cuts off, referring to the tradition that the mothers of High Priests gave food to those in the cities of refuge so they would not pray for the High Priest's death.</note>

**CXLVII.** The text mentions exile, which served as a punishment; however, the death of that **High Priest** was its boundary, not an atonement for the homicide itself. <note>Under Mosaic Law, a person who killed someone accidentally had to remain in a City of Refuge until the death of the High Priest, at which point they were free to go home.</note> If they had possessed **Kings** from the very beginning of the Republic <note>referring to the early Israelite state before the monarchy</note>, perhaps their death would have put an end to the exile. But indeed, I observe that the **Kabbalists** <note>Jewish mystics who look for hidden meanings in the scripture</note> emphasize similar points. For among them, these things are found: **"The term 'nakedness' appears twice in the Masorah to be covered..."** <note>original: ערוה פנים במסורת לכסות (*ervah panim ba-masoret lachasot*)</note>; **"In every instance of 'nakedness' you shall not approach to uncover nakedness,"** which hints that the **priestly garments** atone for acts of incest. That is, the word **nakedness** <note>original: ערוה (*ervah*)</note> occurs only twice according to the **Masorah** <note>The traditional system used to preserve the exact text of the Hebrew Bible</note>: once in Exodus 28:42 and again in Leviticus 18:6; and by this, it is indicated that the priestly vestments provide atonement for sexual sins.

Furthermore, in the same place: **"The Breastplate of Judgment in Gematria indicates atonement for the thoughts of the heart."** <note>original: חשן משפט (*Choshen Mishpat*). <term>Gematria</term> is a mystical method of interpreting Hebrew words based on the numerical value of their letters.</note> And **"Ephod"** <note>A ceremonial vest worn by the High Priest</note> in **Gematria** sounds like **"Angel,"** <note>original: מלאך (*Malach*). In Hebrew, both "Ephod" and "Angel" sum to the value of 91.</note> because the priest was clothed like an **Angel**. And what is said in the same place (Exodus 28:32) regarding **"an opening for his mouth,"** indicates that the priestly **robe** <note>original: pallium / מעיל (*me'il*)</note> atones for the sin of **evil speech** <note>original: לשון הרע (*Lashon Hara*); refers to gossip, slander, or malicious talk</note>. For if someone has committed a sin with an evil tongue, let them make an "opening for their mouth" so that they may be restrained from evil speech, perform repentance, and receive atonement.

<header>CABBALA</header>

In the heart of the day <note>original Hebrew: *be-lev yom*</note> they say that this is a hint toward the law that she [Eve] gave birth only after their sin; **that is, on account of the evil desire <term>Concupiscence|In this context, the *Yetzer Hara* or "evil inclination" which Jewish tradition suggests is an inherent part of human nature, though not identical to the Christian concept of Original Sin</term> implanted in the heart of man, it is just as if he were conceived in sin; and the sense is that from the very birth of man, an evil desire is present within him. CLII. The Rabbi here clearly seems to favor our view <note>The author suggests the Jewish commentator seems to agree with the Christian doctrine of Original Sin</note>; however, he expresses almost a different sense in the Commentary on *Job 14:4*. **"Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean?"** <note>original Hebrew: *tahor mi-tame*</note> is related to: **"Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity, for man is created from an unclean thing."** That is, it is said: *who will give a clean thing from an unclean,* the sense is the same as that other passage: *behold, I was conceived in sin.* For man is produced from an unclean thing <note>This refers to the biological fluids of reproduction, which were considered ritually "unclean" in ancient law</note>. These matters are clarified from the *Talmud, Tractate Niddah, chapter 3,* where this tradition exists: **No woman conceives except near the time of her menstruation, as it is said: "Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity."** That is, no woman <note>original Latin: *nulla puella*</note> conceives except near her menstrual period, because it is said: *behold, I was conceived in sins.* Others express this more clearly, saying that generation occurs **from a putrid drop** <note>original Hebrew: *mi-tippah serukhah*—a common Rabbinic expression for semen emphasizing human humility</note>; for they deny that females would have suffered from the labor of menstruation if sin had not intervened; just as it has no place in beasts, although nothing is lacking for their reproduction.

On page 127, column 4, while dealing with *Psalm 51* and weighing these words, he <note>The commentator being cited</note> supposes that **Jesse was a righteous man** <note>original Hebrew: *ki Yishai hayah tzadik*</note>, that is, that the father of David, *Jesse*, was just, and he adds:

That is to say, there are three ways a man is joined to his wife: first, to satisfy the commandment in *Genesis 1:27–28, "Increase and multiply,"* which method is the best of all. This suggests that the soul of *Adam*, because of the sin committed, has devolved through *metempsychosis* <term>Metempsychosis|The transmigration of a soul into a new body; in Jewish thought, this is known as Gilgul</term> in a continuous series to *David*, and is further to be conferred upon the *Messiah* himself by the same transfer.

CLXII. Frequently, however, they seek reasons by which they might somewhat excuse that shameful deed. The text has it thus, in **Exodus 32:1**: *and the people saw* <gloss>original Hebrew: *boshesh Mosheh*</gloss> *that Moses delayed in coming.* From this arose this gloss: <gloss>The word "delayed" [boshesh] occurs twice: here and in Judges 5:28, "Why is his chariot so long [delayed] in coming?" By <term>Gematria|A system of Jewish numerology where letters of a word correspond to numbers</term>, the verse indicates that Satan showed them his bier, etc.</gloss>

The phrase "he delayed" [boshesh] occurs twice; namely in this place and in **Judges 5:28**. But what is implied in this latter place? That the person of whom it speaks was dead. <note>In Judges 5:28, the mother of the general Sisera waits for him to return from battle, unaware he has been killed; the author argues the word "delay" carries a connotation of death.</note> Thus also the Israelites, in **Exodus 32:1**, thought that Moses was dead: just as the Sages of blessed memory <note>original: *b. m.*, for the Hebrew *zikhrono livrakha*</note> explained, that the appearance of Moses's staff <note>The Latin text uses *baculi* (staff), but the Hebrew legend it cites refers to a *mitah* (bier or coffin). In the story, Satan creates a vision of Moses's coffin in the clouds to trick the people into thinking their leader has died, driving them to create the Golden Calf.</note> was shown to the people in the air. The words themselves show this: *"For this Moses,"* etc., which through **Gematria** coincide with these: *"Satan showed them the staff of Moses, our teacher."* But this is a hollow <note>original: *calva*, literally "bald," meaning a weak or superficial argument.</note> grasping for an excuse and for idolatry.

<insert>The phrase "the power is gone" indicates **exile** through <term>Gematria|A system of Jewish numerology where the letters of a word are totaled to find hidden meanings in words with the same value</term>. By this, it is noted that it will come to pass that the kingdoms [Kings] shall fall [be cast] into Gehenna. For in this way, they substitute abstract terms for concrete ones and swap words among themselves. God’s command is found in **Exodus 25:8**: *Let them make me a sanctuary,* <gloss>original Hebrew: *ve-shakanti*</gloss> *that I may dwell in their midst.* But for how long? <term>R.B.|Likely referring to Rabbi Bachya ben Asher or the "Baal ha-Turim," famous for numerical commentaries</term> believes this is indicated through the letters themselves, in these words:

<insert>The word *ve-shakanti* <gloss>meaning "and I will dwell"</gloss> alludes to the First Temple, and the root "dwell" <gloss>shakan</gloss> is joined with the letters *taf* and *yod* <note>In Hebrew, *taf* = 400 and *yod* = 10, totaling 410</note>. Similarly: *But You are Holy, inhabiting the praises of Israel* <note>Psalm 22:3 in modern Bibles; the text cites Psalm 22:5</note>. The word *Holy* <gloss>original: *Kadosh*</gloss> totals 410. In the same word <gloss>*ve-shakanti*</gloss> are also letters showing the duration of the Second Temple, namely *taf* and *kaf*, which denote the 420 years of the Second Temple's duration.</insert>

That is to say, the word <gloss>original: *dictio*</gloss> וְשָׁכַנְתִּי (*ve-shakanti*) **hints at the First Temple, in which God dwelt for 410 years**; and the same [regarding that word "Holy"] is indicated in **Psalm 22:5**: *You are Holy, inhabiting the praises of Israel.* How long? The word *Holy* <gloss>original: *Kadosh*</gloss> denotes this in numbers, signifying 410; and according to that number of years, His praises were to be sung by the Israelites in the First Temple. Within the very same word, however, are also contained the letters representing the duration of the Second Temple—namely *taf* and *kaf* <note>Hebrew *taf* = 400, *kaf* = 20</note>—which signify the **420 years** the Second Temple lasted.

Similarly, when the First Temple is called a *Mishkan* <gloss>Tabernacle or Dwelling</gloss> and that word in numbers totals 410, they believe the First Temple is again intended. Furthermore, in **Exodus 27:20**, where the word *katit* <gloss>meaning "beaten," referring to olive oil</gloss> implies both 410 and 420 <note>The letters of *katit* can be split into *kaf-taf* (420) and *taf-yod* (410)</note>, they judge this was done so that the duration of both Temples might be determined. One may see **Baal Hatturim** <note>Jacob ben Asher (c. 1269–1343), a pivotal legalist and commentator whose "Baal ha-Turim" commentary is the source of these calculations</note> at the cited passage.
